title: Escrow Administration Standard for Home Mortgage Loans: Payment of Escrowed Bills and Escrow Advances
content:
Escrow on a Home Mortgage Loans note pays the property taxes, the homeowners and flood insurance and the mortgage insurance on the secured property, on or before each bill's due date.

A bill is paid on or before its due date even when the escrow balance is not enough to cover it. Where it is not enough, Piedmont Crescent Bank advances the difference and the escrow balance goes negative by that difference.

A loan on which escrow has been waived has no escrow activity at all.

## Condition, judgement and result

| The escrow balance when a bill falls due | Judgement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Enough to cover the bill | The bill is paid from escrow on or before its due date | The balance falls by the amount of the bill |
| Not enough to cover the bill | The bill is still paid on or before its due date | The bank advances the difference and the balance goes negative |
| The loan has escrow waived | There is no escrow account activity on the loan | No bill is paid from escrow |

## Worked figures on hypothetical inputs

A loan carries an escrow balance of $1400.00 when a property tax bill of $2100.00 falls due. The bill is paid in full on or before its due date, the bank advancing the $700.00 difference, and the escrow balance stands at negative $700.00 afterwards.

The bills escrow pays are of three kinds on a Home Mortgage Loans note: property taxes, homeowners and flood insurance, and mortgage insurance.
